text:
Donald Trump has called for the music performances to be canceled(Image: AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

Donald Trump has called for the crumbling Freedom 250 festival to be canceled just hours after he offered to step in to replace the artists who have dropped out.

As part of his social media spree on Saturday, May 30, the president, 79, said the Great American State Fair should be replaced by a rally of his supporters. Hitting out at the artists who announced they will no longer be part of the lineup, the Republican politician posted on Truth Social, "We should have a giant MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN RALLY, for 250, instead of having overpriced singers, who nobody wants to hear, whose music is boring, and yet who do nothing but complain."

In his post, Trump also hit out at US District Judge Christopher Cooper, who ruled on Friday that the president's name was illegally added to the Kennedy Center and blocked the administration from closing the cultural and arts venue for major renovations. Trump posted over 50 times in seven hours on his social media site on May 30.

Criticizing the judge and calling for the upcoming festival to be canceled, he wrote, "Cancel it, just like I canceled my involvement with the failing and unsafe to be in Kennedy Center, because a Highly Conflicted, Crooked Federal Judge, said that I should not be allowed to spend my time and money in order to MAKE THE CENTER GREAT AGAIN, actually, far greater than it ever was before!

Earlier in the day, the president had offered to perform himself(Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

"It would have also been nice to see a Republican/Democrat union bring it back to life. The Kennedy Center is broken, unsafe, and $busted, and has been for many years!"

He continued, "Judge Cooper also stated that the highly prestigious Board of the Center was not authorized to add on the name 'TRUMP' despite the fact that hundreds of millions of dollars of my time and money will be necessary for its successful reincarnation. So now, the Kennedy Center will collapse, both structurally and financially.

"Judge Cooper and his wife, Amy Jeffress (obfuscation anyone?), should be ashamed of themselves. Judge Cooper, like numerous other Crooked Judges on my cases, should be IMPEACHED. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN! President DONALD J. TRUMP."

Bret Michaels said he won't perform during Freedom 250(Image: Getty Images for SiriusXM)

The Great American State Fair, scheduled to take place on Washington D.C.'s National Mall, has seen several performers withdraw shortly after the initial lineup was announced by Freedom 250. In response, the president said he was considering stepping in to replace the departing artists.

Writing in a lengthy post on Truth Social on Saturday, Trump suggested he could headline the event himself. "I understand Artists are getting 'the yips' having to do with their performance on Wednesday, so I am thinking about bringing the Number One Attraction anywhere in the World, the man who gets much larger audiences than Elvis in his prime, and he does so without a guitar, the man who loves our Country more than anyone else, and the man who some say is the Greatest President in History (THE GOAT!), DONALD J. TRUMP, to take the place of these highly paid, Third Rate 'Artists,' and give a major speech, rallying the Country forward like I have done ever since being President!" he wrote.

Martina McBride is one of the artists who have dropped out(Image: Penske Media via Getty Images)

However, just hours later he called for the festival to be canceled. The concert lineup was first announced on Wednesday, May 27, by Freedom 250, an organization that describes itself as a nonpartisan public-private partnership focused on commemorating the anniversary year. The initial list of performers included Martina McBride, Flo Rida, Vanilla Ice, Young MC, C+C Music Factory, Milli Vanilli, the Commodores and Bret Michaels.

However, by Wednesday evening, Morris Day and the Time addressed speculation about their involvement. "Morris Day & the Time will not be performing at the 'Great American State Fair,'" Day wrote on Instagram, adding in the caption, "It's A No For Me." Also that night, Young MC said on social media that he would not be performing.

Members of the Commodores, Martina and Bret all joined in on announcing they would not perform. Meanwhile, a group performing as Real Milli Vanilli said it would not appear at the event, though Fab Morvan confirmed he still plans to perform.
